messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: high error rate from text-gen service in us-west-2. 5xx spike, latency up >3x. Auto-escalation to #eng-oncall.

sam: I'm on it, taking the pager. Any customer-facing tickets yet?

maria: We already have increased 502s for a handful of customers (cust-342, cust-778). CS reported degraded completions starting ~10:12 UTC.

devops-ryan: Looking at infra metrics — GPU pool 'gpool-usw2-3' GPU utilization is at 98% and queue depth for text-gen is at 9k requests. HPA shows desired pods increased but node provisioning stalled.

sam: Can you paste the HPA events and node pool autoscaler events?

devops-ryan: Events snippet: 
```
Normal  ScalingReplicaSet  3m (x3 over 5m)  horizontal-pod-autoscaler  New size: 48; reason: CPU above target
Warning  FailedScheduling  2m  default-scheduler  0/24 nodes are available: 24 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
```

kate: So HPA wanted to scale pods but nodes with GPUs weren't available. Looks like the cloud autoscaler didn't request more GPU nodes because of a quota/label mismatch. Checking autoscaler logs now.

maria: Timeline so far: 10:08 deploy of text-gen v2.1 (config increased concurrency). 10:11 sudden increase in requests (A/B experiment ramp). 10:12 error spike observed by CS. 10:15 HPA fired. 10:17 scheduler started failing to place pods. 10:20 GPU pool saturated.

sam: Live mitigation options: 1) Temporarily route traffic from prod-usw2 to prod-usw2-fallback pool (lower perf but available). 2) Increase pool min nodes / request manual quota bump. 3) Roll back v2.1 if traffic ramp is culprit. Which is fastest?

devops-ryan: Quickest is routing traffic away. I can flip the routing rule in the edge LB to send 30% to fallback. That should drop queue depth. Also I'll patch the HPA to lower target CPU to force more pod autoscaling while we sort out nodes. Patch: 
```sh
kubectl -n text-gen patch hpa text-gen --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/metrics/0/resource/targetAverageUtilization","value":50}]'
```

kate: FYI the node autoscaler logs show a failing API call to the cloud provider: 403 QuotaExceeded for GPU cores in region. That explains provisioning stall. Raising a quota request is in flight, but not immediate.

maria: I'll notify CS/ops with current mitigation: routing + HPA patch + warmup preloads to fallback. Copying status to incident ticket INC-8721.

sam: Can someone run a warmup job to avoid cold starts on new nodes? We see model loading is ~7-10s per worker which compounds queue latency. Suggest synthetic warmups: 100 warmup requests across new pods.

devops-ryan: K kicking off warmup job: 
```sh
kubectl -n text-gen run warmup-job --image=tools/warmup:latest --restart=OnFailure -- /bin/warmup --target text-gen.prod --requests 200
```

oncall-bot: action logged: routed 30% traffic to fallback pool at 10:28 UTC by devops-ryan. HPA patched at 10:30 UTC. Warmup job started 10:32 UTC.

kate: After routing, queue depth dropped from 9k to 2.5k and errors are trending down. Latency still elevated due to warmup.

sam: Good. For RCA tracking, propose hypotheses: 
H1: Node autoscaler failed due to GPU quota exhaustion (evidence: 403 QuotaExceeded in autoscaler logs).
H2: New deployment increased per-pod concurrency leading to more pods desired; combined with HPA config, triggered faster scale than infra could handle.
H3: Metrics lag in metrics-server caused delayed HPA decisioning (we saw several stale CPU datapoints in 10:14-10:17 window).

maria: Adding logs and traces to the ticket. Attaching scheduler logs and autoscaler trace IDs: asc-zzx-119.

devops-ryan: Also discovered node pool taint mismatch: new GPU nodes use label gpu-type=ampere but our nodeSelector requested gpu-type=tesla for some pods in the new deployment - that caused scheduling gaps. I'm adding that as H4 (misconfigured nodeSelector after deploy).

sam: Nice find. That explains some pods bouncing between Pending and FailedScheduling. Can you paste the pod describe error?

devops-ryan: Pod describe snippet: 
```
Events:
  Warning FailedScheduling  2m (x12 over 8m)  default-scheduler  0/24 nodes are available: 24 node(s) didn't match node selector.
```

kate: Action items (live and post-incident):
- Live: keep routing to fallback until quota resolved or we increase min nodes (devops-ryan)
- Live: run warmup (devops-ryan)
- Live: monitor error rate and CS impact (maria)
- RCA: investigate deployment config change that altered nodeSelector/concurrency (sam)
- RCA: confirm autoscaler 403 -> quota change + timeline and request support from cloud (kate)

maria: CS note: we informed affected customers, offering AP credits; only a subset saw failures — majority saw higher latency but completed.

sam: Handoff: I'm heading to dinner soon, leaving followup to kate for the teardown and next-step infra changes. kate, please escalate quota req if ETA is >1hr. I'll update the incident ticket with the hypotheses and timeline.

kate: On it. I'll own next-hour ops and loop in cloud support and infra. Also will file an internal bug for the deploy-time nodeSelector regression.

oncall-bot: oncall handoff recorded: sam -> kate at 10:45 UTC. Incident status: mitigated (errors decreasing), monitoring.

maria: Final note: we should add a preflight check to deploy pipeline validating nodeSelector labels vs pool labels and assert GPU quota before big ramps. Filing doc ticket DOC-514. :+1:

sam: Thanks all. Leaving the channel.
